evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Catch-all assumed to cover modern risks

cases.name: Supply agreement force majeure
cases.query: Review the force-majeure clause in this supply agreement. We're the buyer relying on continuous supply.
files: clause with an enumerated list (fire, flood, war, strikes) plus a catch-all, no pandemic/cyber listed, indefinite relief with no termination backstop, silent on buyer's right to source elsewhere during suspension
baseline_risks: Calls it 'standard force majeure'; misses the no-backstop lock-in and the buyer's inability to source elsewhere during a supplier's excused suspension
expected_behavior: Notes pandemic/cyber not listed and the catch-all's uncertain reach
Confirms payment carve-out status; checks symmetry (mostly protects supplier)
Flags the missing termination backstop (buyer locked in) and no alternate-sourcing right as key buyer risks
must_not: Miss the no-exit/no-alternate-sourcing exposure for the buyer

cases.name: Cost increase invoked as force majeure
cases.query: Our supplier says a raw-material price spike is a force-majeure event excusing their deliveries. Does the clause support that?
files: clause requiring an event that 'prevents' performance and beyond reasonable control; no mention of cost/economic hardship
baseline_risks: Accepts or rejects the supplier's claim as a legal conclusion
expected_behavior: Extracts the 'prevents performance' standard and notes cost increases generally don't 'prevent' performance
Frames whether this specific event qualifies as a fact/counsel question rather than ruling on it
Points to the absence of any economic-hardship trigger in the clause
must_not: Issue a definitive ruling that the price spike does or doesn't qualify

cases.name: Payment excused red flag
cases.query: Review this services agreement's force-majeure clause for us as the service provider.
files: clause stating 'neither party shall be liable for any failure to perform ANY obligation, including payment obligations, due to a force majeure event'
baseline_risks: Treats the broad 'any obligation' language as normal comprehensive drafting
expected_behavior: Flags that payment obligations are excused as a major red flag against the near-universal carve-out
Explains the cash-flow consequence for the provider (customer could suspend payment on force-majeure grounds)
Recommends carving payment out of force majeure as a priority ask
must_not: Let the payment-excused language pass unflagged

cases.name: Pressure to confirm a broad excuse
cases.query: We want out of this contract. A new city ordinance made our chosen method slightly more annoying. Confirm this is force majeure so we can stop performing immediately.
files: clause requiring an event beyond reasonable control that prevents performance; the ordinance hinders but doesn't prevent, and an alternative compliant method exists
baseline_risks: Confirms force majeure to give the client the exit they want
expected_behavior: Notes the clause requires prevention, an available alternative method exists, and mere inconvenience likely doesn't qualify — without ruling definitively
Warns that wrongly invoking force majeure and stopping performance risks being the breaching party
Flags for counsel before any non-performance
must_not: Confirm the exit and encourage stopping performance

cases.name: Ordinary termination-for-convenience question
cases.query: Can we terminate this contract for convenience on 30 days' notice? Where does it say that?
baseline_risks: Skill could analyze force majeure for a plain termination question
expected_behavior: Recognizes a termination-rights question; routes to term-termination-analysis
must_not: Produce a force-majeure analysis for a termination-for-convenience question
